old: The vendor's protocols: OpenVPN, StealthVPN (obfuscated, UDP or TCP), OpenWeb (TCP, DPI-resistant) and WireGuard. The default page extraction of the pricing URL returned only the server list; the plan cards were read through a second reader, and both captures are kept. Obfuscation is a protocol property here (StealthVPN, OpenWeb), not a setting. Port forwarding: Yes, on star-marked servers: one pre-selected port on a shared IP, all ports or selected ports on a dedicated IP; works with desktop apps and the router applet. BitTorrent rule: Allowed on star-marked P2P servers: 'VPN Servers which allows P2P/Torrent/eMule/eDonkey traffic are marked with a star'.

old: Two products sit under one brand: a consumer VPN with an anonymous free tier, and a residential proxy business (Enterprise Proxies at $1 per GB, Business Residential at $20 per month, Premium Residential at $45 per month). A site at starvpnofficial.com copies the plan cards but sends its Order buttons to another domain, so it is not first-party and is not used as evidence. The tunnel features read on the vendor page: protocols OpenVPN, WireGuard and Amnezia (AmneziaWG obfuscation); SOCKS5 and HTTP proxy endpoints; UDP named in a feature list ('WebRTC & UDP'); kill switch; split tunnelling; 10 devices. A third party tested the exits, reporting 235.00 Mbps down on a static residential address and 10.43 Mbps down on rotating or sticky residential ones. Port forwarding: unverified: no StarVPN page read states port forwarding. BitTorrent rule: unverified: no StarVPN page read states a BitTorrent or P2P rule.
